Precondition fails: the deck deals exactly one item at a time (src/features/agents/quick-answer/triage/deck/useDeckControls.tsx:158) and offers no multi-select, so no single judgment can cover many items.

pairs.registryProposal: This pairing is a vocabulary collision, not a coverage hole. The matcher scored `adoption-measurement` against a context whose directory is literally named `adoption/` but whose subject is a template-instantiation wizard. Routing by the golden path's precondition — 'you are measuring other people's behaviour, observed at second hand, across a stated eligible population' — rejects it immediately, where routing by the word 'adoption' accepts it. Suggest the map-builder demote lexical matches on a subject's own headline noun when the golden path's stated precondition is population-level measurement and the context has no population; and that these two contexts be re-paired against a form/wizard subject in ui-surfaces or client-architecture.

pairs.subject: realtime-events
pairs.evidence: src/hooks/realtime/useRealtimeEvents.ts:112 builds the displayed list and its derived stats purely from pushed payloads with no authoritative read path, so a counted drop or a late mount produces a confidently wrong events-per-minute and success rate that nothing heals

techniques.evidence: src/hooks/realtime/createSingletonListener.ts:96-100 drops the newest early arrival once the 50-entry buffer is full and keeps the oldest — the inverse of the newest-retained rule, so a consumer attaching milliseconds late replays a stale prefix and misses exactly the recent transitions the buffer exists to close the race on; :57-60 also fans out over the live subscriber Set rather than a snapshot, leaving mid-dispatch detach behaviour undefined rather than decided. The rest is strong: one native listener per name, teardown that handles the in-flight handshake (:109-115,:120-130), and counted evictions with a named channel (:65-76).

src/hooks/realtime/createSingletonListener.ts:39,103 hold the frame buffer as a list rather than a keyed map, so N facts about one entity in a burst are applied N times instead of collapsing by supersession; and when the last consumer detaches (:163-168) the pending frameQueue is neither flushed nor counted as discarded — the scheduled rAF at :52-62 fires into an empty subscriber set and the batch vanishes silently, the same shed-without-counting hole the golden path forbids.

src/lib/eventRegistry.ts:30 is a genuine closed vocabulary with a Rust mirror and a real parity gate (scripts/check-event-registry.mjs:34-51, reading both live artifacts), but src/hooks/realtime/useRunEventListener.ts:60,83 accepts a free-text `eventName` and calls raw `listen`, and the gate only diffs the two name lists — it never asserts it found the emit/subscribe sites, so an off-registry subscription is invisible to it and presents at runtime as 'nothing happened'. src/lib/eventRegistry.ts:5 also names `src-tauri/src/engine/event_registry.rs` as the mirrored authority; that file does not exist.

src/hooks/realtime/useRealtimeEvents.ts:112 initializes from an empty array and never reads the persona-events store; :189 applies each pushed payload as state with an unchecked `as RealtimeEvent` cast, and :67-108 derives eventsPerMinute and successRate from that push-only window — so the two drops the hook honestly counts (:113-114,:157) degrade the display from late to wrong, with no refetch-on-mount, on-focus or periodic sweep to heal them.
Precondition fails: storage-level change hooks, transaction staging and the bounded capture channel live in the backend; this context holds only frontend consumers of an already-published bus.

Precondition fails: src/hooks/realtime/useSmeeRelayStatus.ts and useCloudWebhookRelay.ts render a relay's status payload; the durable-watermark pull loop, per-tick caps and dead-letter records they report on are implemented in src-tauri, not here.

pairs.subject: web-scraping
pairs.evidence: src/features/scraper/useScrapeForm.ts:13-23 has no failure-semantics member on a rule, so no field can be required and extraction collapse is indistinguishable from a quiet day — and ScrapeEditorWizard.tsx:84 lets an unpreviewed rule set save armed

techniques.evidence: src/features/scraper/useScrapeForm.ts:13-23 declares target field, locator and (for css only) cardinality but omits the technique's mandatory failure-semantics member and any post-processing step, so no rule set can declare a required field and the subject's honesty law has no instrument to stand on; field names are free text (:29,:65) rather than drawn from a dataset schema, and :65 silently drops any rule whose name is blank instead of failing at a validation door — `canSave` (:154) never checks that a selector parses, a regex compiles or a pointer is well-formed. The flat-editable-form-serialized-only-at-the-edges rule is realized well (:51-68).

src/features/scraper/LlmRuleBuilder.tsx:74 advertises 'No URL yet — Claude will infer from your description' and :33 passes a possibly-undefined `urls[0]`, so rules can be authored from the model's imagination rather than the real fetched page — the precise failure the technique names; :39 then adopts the proposal into the form on a bare non-empty-count check, with no execution against the authoring page, no per-rule verification shown to the human, no fetch/time/digest provenance stamp, and replace-vs-merge chosen automatically rather than as an informed human act.

The preview itself has all four properties — src/features/scraper/EditorSteps.tsx:127 runs the edited rules against the live URLs through the production `scraper_preview_extract` and writes nothing — but the gate does not exist: src/features/scraper/ScrapeEditorWizard.tsx:84 disables Save only on `!form.canSave`, and the step rail at :43 lets the author jump straight past Preview to Schedule and save; src/features/scraper/useScrapeForm.ts:121 defaults `enabled` to true, so never-previewed rules enter the scheduler armed rather than as marked-unverified drafts.

src/features/scraper/useScraperData.ts:179-187 derives a run's health by prefix-matching a free-text `lastStatus` string, so a run that fetched successfully and extracted nothing renders as a green pill (src/features/scraper/ScraperControlRoom.tsx:132,204); there are no per-rule hit counts, no baseline from the authoring preview, no record-count expectation, and no collapse, quarantine or re-authoring state anywhere on the operator surface.

src/features/scraper/useScrapeForm.ts:163 makes `key_field` optional and :154 omits it from `canSave`, so a scrape can be created with a dataset and no identity key — re-scraping the same page then has nothing to reconcile against and appends rather than updating, which is the dataset corruption the technique exists to prevent.

src/features/scraper/EditorSteps.tsx:192-199 accepts a raw 5-field cron string with no validation and no minimum-cadence floor, and neither the step nor useScrapeForm.ts:164 surfaces any politeness posture — nothing prevents a per-minute schedule against a third-party host, and the guest obligations the golden path states are absent from the one surface where cadence is chosen.

Precondition fails: the technique governs the rollout of a shape-change detector from observing to consequential, and no detector exists anywhere in this system (see shape-change-detection above) — there are no stored verdicts to replay and no consequences to place behind a flag.
